title: OSCON 2010:  Rob Pike, "Public Static Void"
summary: A 13-minute OSCON 2010 talk in which Rob Pike argues about what is wrong with mainstream languages like C++, Java and C#, and presents Go as a response. He discusses verbosity and what lightness means in a language.
why: HN uses it as a concise statement of the thinking behind Go's design.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: gave this short speech at OSCON 2010 about what's wrong with programming languages, their thinking, and their recent direction
